messages:
alex: Heads-up — I ran a short nsys sample on staging to investigate a 95th latency bump. Wanted to share a low-impact profiling playbook draft and get feedback.

mira: Nice. Can you paste the commands you used? want to check overhead assumptions.

alex: Sure — kept it to 30s and used sampling with nvtx markers around the runtime request handler. Command: 
```
nsys profile -t cuda,osrt --sample=cpu --output=tmp_preface \
  --trace-fork-before-exec=true \
  --sample-interval=1000us \
  --force-overwrite --capture-range=nvtx:start,nvtx:end \
  <run-staging-load>
```
I added NVTX push/pop in the handler: nvtxRangePushA("handle_request")/nvtxRangePop.

jon: FYI sampling interval looks fine for a quick scan. What overhead did you see?

alex: End-to-end p95 for the traced requests increased from 120ms -> 140ms (≈16%). CPU usage bumped slightly on the host. Kernel timelines were readable; we saw a mis-selection where the runtime picked an FP16 kernel that regressed for long sequences.

sarah: 16% is a bit high for staging but acceptable as an exploratory run. For prod we should aim <5% impact. Any ideas to lower it?

alex: That's the point of the playbook: low-impact tiers. Proposal:
- Tier A (quick): 15-60s sampling via nsys with capture-range=nvtx and a coarse sample interval (1ms+). safe for staging.
- Tier B (targeted): 2-5min runs with sampling + selective env vars (RT_PROF_KERNELS=1) and NVTX only around suspect code. Limit to canary hosts.
- Tier C (deep): full instrumented trace (nsys full trace / nvprof) only in non-prod or air-gapped bench nodes. Not allowed in shared prod.

mira: +1. Also add guardrails: a test run to measure baseline overhead (no traces) and one short trace to calculate delta. If delta >5% for prod canary, abort.

jon: We should formalize the abort thresholds and automated rollback for canaries. E.g., if tracing increases tail latency by >5% for 5 consecutive minutes, disable tracing and send alert.

alex: Agreed. I sketched an automated probe: start short sampling window, compute p90/p95 delta vs baseline in CloudWatch, revert sampling flag via /ops API if exceeded.

perf-bot: reminder: tracing toggles are auditable. Please include ticket reference and justification when enabling Tier B/C.

sarah: One more thing — kernel selection: the sampling runs exposed a kernel switch at ~350 tokens where the runtime chose a different matmul kernel. We need to capture kernel names in the NVTX metadata and map to our kernel catalog. Proposed snippet to log kernel meta: 
```cpp
// inside kernel selection path
nvtxNameOsThreadA("kernel_select");
LOG(INFO) << "kernel=" << chosen_kernel_id << " seq_len=" << seq_len;
```
That ties a kernel name to the nvtx interval.

mira: Good. Also add a KV-cache sampling tip: enable small percentage of requests to exercise cache hits/misses with tracing off for others. That gives representative behavior without full trace overhead.

alex: Right — our A/B sampler can flip a header X-RI-PROF-SAMPLE. Keep sample rate <=1% in prod by default. For canary we can bump to 5-10%.

jon: Any numbers on nsys overhead vs pure sampling? We should document expected ranges per tier.

alex: From quick experiments:
- nsys sampling (1ms interval, NVTX capture-range): ~5-20% end-to-end overhead depending on host load and kernel density.
- coarse sampling (5ms+): ~2-8% but with less resolution.
- full trace (complete capture): 50%+ — unacceptable in shared prod.

sarah: Let's include a short checklist in the playbook:
1) Baseline run (no profiling) — collect 5min metrics.
2) Tier A run 30-60s — check p90/p95 delta.
3) If Tier A shows anomaly, run Tier B on canary hosts with KV-sampler and NVTX markers, 2-5min.
4) If kernel hotspots found, annotate kernel-catalog and schedule targeted quant/kerning work.
5) For dev-only deep dives use full trace nodes.

mira: Also note limitations: sampling can miss rare thread preemption issues and short-lived kernels. Add guidance to use perfetto or syscall tracing for those cases.

alex: I updated the draft playbook in the shared doc (link: https://rwd.company/s/low-impact-profiler-playbook). TL;DR: don't run full traces on shared prod, keep sample rates low, NVTX markers and short capture ranges, automated rollback at +5% tail delta.

jon: This looks actionable. Can we add an example CloudWatch query to compute p95 delta?

alex: Example (pseudo): 
```
SELECT percentile(latency_p95, 95) FROM RequestMetrics WHERE env='canary' AND trace_flag=0 as baseline
SELECT percentile(latency_p95, 95) FROM RequestMetrics WHERE env='canary' AND trace_flag=1 as traced
compute delta = (traced - baseline) / baseline
alert if delta > 0.05 for 5m
```
perf-bot: prod-tracing-policy reminder: Tier B requires ops approval for non-canary prod hosts.

sarah: I'll turn this into an RFC/ops-runbook and ping infra for the automated rollback hook. Alex — can you attach the sample traces (nsys .qdrep) and a short summary in the RFC?

alex: Will do. Uploading the trimmed .qdrep to the artifact bucket and will post links in the RFC. Thanks for the feedback — will iterate and then we can onboard it to the runbook. :thumbsup:
